"Horrid" is an exaggeration, but some perspective would probably go a long way here. If you are happily selling something for days at a high price and people are buying it at a healthy rate, then someone comes and starts flooding supply with listings almost half that price, then suddenly you aren't able to sell that item -at all- unless you want to sell it at half the efficiency you were before. Many people aren't willing to do this, especially since there is no promise at all that they won't undercut you again in a similar fashion. That is often not worth your time, and having to scout out new markets over this is aggravating, especially if the item in question is rare and isn't the most in demand (as is often the case on lower population servers, where, yes, this sort of undercutting is extremely damaging to sellers.)

There's also the issue of item worth. You say it only costs a small amount to make, but this is not the only factor. You spent time and resources leveling crafters to be able to make this item. What is your time worth? What about the currency you spent to level that craft? Just because it costs me basically nothing to craft a specific item doesn't mean it's appropriate to sell it for a trivial amount.

Finally, a lot of people are simply too lazy to make items themselves, or have largely expendable amounts of currency. Demand defines itself--who are you to decide what an item is worth over the people buying it?

Look, it's not okay for people to harass you over markets, but I think your attitudes would annoy a majority of less confrontational sellers off.

* It's important to note that you have to have the trash **in front** of the cannons. Also, usually a DPS or Healer or even the off-tank activate the search light while the trash is being killed by cannons.
* For the colossi especially, the tank should be ready to stun enemies out of their AoEs to the best of their ability so the cannons don't get destroyed.
* There's a second set of cannons to pull everything to in this step that is neglected.
* "Pulling the boss" isn't super intuitive here. You stand on the ramp on the far right end of the room as you enter. When a certain character arrives, a few enemies will spawn. After several more moments, the actual boss spawns. The main tank stays on the boss the entire time and ignores all the adds, which usually get AoEd out of existence before they're a problem.
* As far as average groups, I have never once seen them tank the boss on the character.
* It's worth noting that if the cannons were destroyed in this next part, you have to go back to the second set of cannons instead.

Also, throughout these dungeon trash pull instructions, be **Sprinting,** especially on the last pull. If a healer didn't come with you on the last pull, you will probably need cooldowns to stay alive while you make your way back to the cannons.

* **For another dungeon,** "pull the trash and use the console" is very literal. Unless someone is trying to heal you, when you aggro the trash then touch the console, it stays aggro'd on you even though you're on another floor and won't attack your party members assuming they don't get on the aggro table. Detailed cross class tips:

**Provoke: Mandatory.** If someone grabs aggro off you, it can easily be immensely sloppier fighting to get back on top without this ability. It is 100% required in raid encounters at end game that require you to swap tanks--you are literally unable to do so without it. Motivate yourself to get your tank class to level 22 for it ASAP.

**Flash:** Generates enmity in a circle around you at the cost of MP, a resource you use for nothing else. You'll learn that Overpower (especially on the leveling track) can really hurt your TP over time, and this ability helps you keep aggro while getting some TP back. You can use it after being Pacified from Berserk. It can help at the start of a pull when you are trying to position enemies because it is a circle around you and not just a cone in front of you like Overpower. When you are experienced and confident in your ability to manage your TP and enmity, you can free up this slot with something else as it is not especially necessary in any particular scenario.

**Convalescence:** Increases healing received from spells by 20%. When you unlock your warrior class at level 30, your tank stance increases your healing received by 20%. This ability synergizes excellently with what you're already doing as a warrior. A smart healer will change what they're doing when they see this, because it allows them to heal less. It's a good tanking cooldown.

**Awareness:** Reduces your chance to be critically hit to 0. This is a good ability to use on trash, but a lot of bosses don't crit. Can substantially reduce damage on trash pulls. Later it synergizes with one of your high-level cooldowns that reduces damage you take from the front by 20%, but increases your chance to be critically hit from the flank and rear by 100%. Awareness removes the drawback from this cooldown completely. If you're fighting a single boss with no adds that cannot crit, this ability doesn't really do much because you shouldn't ever be getting hit in the flank or back by a single enemy, thus negating its usefulness even for Raw Intuition.

**Internal Release:** Increases your critical chance by 10%. While this may seem like a simple DPS cooldown, it synergizes well with a lot of your abilities as it affects not only your attacks but also the self-heals Equilibrium and Second Wind. You always want to try to pair it with Berserk, but you will not always since its cooldown is shorter.

**Second Wind:** A modest self heal. This is usually your last pick for cross class as it can be somewhat low impact and pales in comparison to Equilibrium when you have it. It synergizes very strongly with Berserk because it scales with your attack power, which Berserk increases by 50%. If you're going to use it, try to have Berserk (and Internal Release ideally) up first if it's available to maximize its effectiveness.

**Mantra:** Increases healing received by 5% for you and anyone else near you when you cast it. At a fourth of the effectiveness of Convalescence, this isn't likely to have a meaningful impact and is best left to the DPSers who have nothing better to take.

**Featherfoot:** Increases dodge chance by 12%. This doesn't work on bosses' tankbusters and otherwise is simply not a very effective mitigation cooldown. It could have a better footprint on big trash pulls, but if you're considering using it for that, just take Awareness instead.

**Haymaker:** Chance to do an attack barely stronger than Heavy Swing with no real benefits. Garbage.

**Savage Blade:** Unless you like 100 potency weaponskills, you literally can't use this. Maybe put it on outside one of the major cities just to see its animation.

A typical cross class lineup is Provoke, Flash, Convalescence, Internal Release, then either Awareness or Second Wind based on what your needs are. If you don't need Flash, take both Awareness and Second Wind.

This creates a conflict of interest, and you might get a different answer for what people want out of dungeons when posed with two different versions of roughly the same question.

I think there's a middle ground where developers can do just about anything to make four-player content more interesting, and my concern is when this concept gets combined with "make them more challenging." Here again you have two conflicting interests: desiring challenging four-player content and wanting the specific game mode to be less tedious.
